concept_mcqs.stem:
You inherit a query meant to push the date filter to SQL Server, but performance is poor. Current M steps:

```powerquery
let
    Source = Sql.Database("bi-sql", "Sales"),
    dbo_FactSales = Source{[Schema="dbo", Item="FactSales"]}[Data],
    Buffered = Table.Buffer(dbo_FactSales),
    Filtered = Table.SelectRows(Buffered, each [OrderDate] >= #date(2026, 1, 1)),
    KeptCols = Table.SelectColumns(Filtered, {"OrderDate","ProductID","Qty"})
in
    KeptCols
```
On refresh, which change ensures the date filter is executed by SQL Server (query folding preserved for the filter)?
options: Replace `Table.Buffer` with `Table.FromRows` to force a new table that folds.
Keep `Buffered` but move it after `KeptCols` so fewer rows are buffered before filtering.
Add `Table.AddIndexColumn` before the filter so the engine can track row order before pushing predicates down.
Remove the `Buffered` step and filter directly on `dbo_FactSales` before any non-folding operation.
concept_mcqs.explanation: `Table.Buffer` materializes data and blocks folding for subsequent steps. Removing it allows the filter on `OrderDate` to fold back to SQL. Folding occurs up to the first non-folding step. Filtering early on the native source preserves predicate pushdown.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B is tempting because buffering fewer columns feels cheaper, but any `Table.Buffer` prior to the filter still prevents folding the filter. C sounds technical but `Table.FromRows` creates an in-memory table and also prevents folding. D is a common misunderstanding; adding an index is non-folding and at best further blocks folding; it does not help predicate pushdown.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You import a CSV with UK-style dates and accept the default `Changed Type` step. Sample rows:

```csv
OrderID,OrderDate,Amount
101,05/03/2026,120.50
102,13/03/2026,89.99
```
Power Query uses the `en-US` locale by default. After the type change to Date, what will happen to the two `OrderDate` values?
options: Both remain text because Power Query refuses to change type without an explicit locale.
`05/03/2026` becomes May 3, 2026; `13/03/2026` becomes an error.
`05/03/2026` becomes 5 March 2026; `13/03/2026` becomes 13 March 2026 (both correct).
Both become errors because the slash-delimited format is ambiguous.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Under the default `en-US` locale, `05/03/2026` is interpreted as MM/DD/YYYY (May 3). `13/03/2026` is invalid as a month 13 and turns into an error. The fix is to use `Using Locale...` with an en-GB locale or parse via `Date.FromText` with a culture.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A is what you'd get with en-GB, not en-US. C is plausible but Power Query will try to convert and only error on invalid rows. D is false; Power Query eagerly applies the default locale when changing types.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Profiling shows `City` has 4 distinct values, but business says all are "NY". Sample values show visually identical entries:

```text
NY
NY 
NY 
ny
```
Which transformation sequence will correctly collapse these to a single value?
options: Apply `Transform > Format > Lowercase` only.
Apply `Transform > Format > Trim` only.
Apply `Clean`, then `Trim`, then `Lowercase` on `City`.
Apply `Transform > Format > Clean` only.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Non-breaking spaces require `Clean` to remove non-printables; trailing spaces require `Trim`; and case variance requires `Lowercase`. The sequence yields a single canonical value.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A trims regular spaces but not non-breaking spaces or case. B removes non-printables but leaves trailing spaces and case. C unifies case but leaves whitespace differences. Only the combined sequence resolves all three discrepancies.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You combine monthly CSV exports from a folder. Power Query auto-generates helper queries:

```text
Queries
  Transform Sample File
  Sample File
  Sample File Parameter
  Archived Sales (folder)
  Archived Sales
```
After you add column type changes in `Archived Sales`, new files keep coming in with raw types. Where should you move the type-change steps so they apply to every file consistently?
options: Edit `Sample File` to add type changes; that file is the template.
Keep type changes in `Archived Sales`; they propagate automatically.
Add a `Changed Type` step after `Expanded Table Column` in `Archived Sales (folder)`.
Move type changes into `Transform Sample File` so the function applies them per file during combine.
concept_mcqs.explanation: The combine pattern uses `Transform Sample File` as a function applied to each file. Placing type and cleanup steps there ensures every file receives identical transformations at combine time.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A is a common misconception; steps in the final query after expansion won't update how each file is transformed. C only affects the single sample file, not the function. D changes types after expansion but leaves per-file transforms inconsistent and brittle.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You must list customers with no orders in the last 30 days. Given:

```csv
-- Customers.csv --
CustomerID,Name
1,Ada Co
2,Beta LLC
3,Calix

-- Orders.csv --
OrderID,CustomerID,OrderDate
10,1,2026-03-01
11,1,2026-03-25
12,2,2026-02-10
```
Assume today is 2026-03-31 and `Orders` is already filtered to last 30 days in a separate query. Which merge produces the required list?
options: Left Outer join `Customers` to filtered `Orders`, then keep rows where `Orders.OrderID` is null.
Right Outer join filtered `Orders` to `Customers`, then keep rows where `Customers.CustomerID` is null.
Left Anti join `Customers` to filtered `Orders`.
Inner join `Customers` to filtered `Orders`, then de-duplicate customers.
concept_mcqs.explanation: A Left Anti join directly returns rows from the left table (Customers) with no match on the right (filtered last-30-days Orders), which is the cleanest solution.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A works but requires an extra filtering step and is error-prone if null checks are missed. B returns orders with no matching customers, the inverse of what you need. D yields only customers with orders, the opposite set.

concept_mcqs.stem:
A requirement states: "The dashboard shows KPI 'Average Ticket Resolution Time' at an hourly grain, updated daily." Available fields from the source ticketing system extract are:

```text
TicketID
CreatedAt (datetime)
FirstResponseAt (datetime)
ClosedAt (datetime, can be null)
AssignedAgent
Status
```
Which computation in Power Query best aligns with the requirement while avoiding bias from still-open tickets?
options: Compute `(ClosedAt - CreatedAt)` but filter to `Status = Closed` before averaging.
Use `(Now() - CreatedAt)` for open tickets and `(ClosedAt - CreatedAt)` for closed tickets, then average together.
Compute `(ClosedAt - CreatedAt)` for all rows; nulls will be ignored in the average automatically.
Compute `(FirstResponseAt - CreatedAt)` for all rows to avoid nulls.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Averaging only fully resolved tickets aligns with "Resolution Time" and avoids skew from open items. Including open tickets with null `ClosedAt` either errors or is dropped inconsistently. Filtering to closed tickets is explicit and defensible in the spec.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A assumes nulls are harmless; they either error or get dropped without documentation. C measures response, not resolution, changing the KPI definition. D mixes durations of different semantics and inflates averages as long-open tickets accumulate.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Your `Sales` query shows the gear icon "Source" step:

```powerquery
Source = Csv.Document(File.Contents("C:\\Users\\Analyst\\Downloads\\Sales_2026_03.csv"),[Delimiter=",", Columns=5, Encoding=65001, QuoteStyle=QuoteStyle.None])
```
The team shares the PBIX and others cannot refresh. Without introducing Power BI Service, which edit makes this query portable across analysts' machines?
options: Switch to the Web connector and host the CSV on any public URL.
Replace the absolute path with a parameterized folder path and build the file path from it.
Keep the absolute path and instruct others to copy the file to the same location.
Use `Data Source Settings` to "Ignore privacy levels" so everyone can refresh.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Parameterizing the root folder and constructing the file path from it removes machine-specific absolute paths. Peers can point the parameter to their local or network location.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B introduces a different source and governance issues not in scope. C is brittle and not a proper requirement-level solution. D addresses privacy isolation, not portability; it does not fix the hard-coded path.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You need a monthly KPI that compares actuals to targets. Data:

```csv
-- Actuals.csv (daily) --
OrderDate,Amount
2026-03-01,120
2026-03-02,80

-- Targets.csv (monthly) --
Month,TargetAmount
2026-03,6000
```
A colleague proposes merging on formatted month name:

```powerquery
Actuals = Table.AddColumn(Actuals, "MonthName", each Date.ToText([OrderDate], "MMMM")),
Targets = Table.TransformColumns(Targets, {{"Month", each Date.MonthName(Date.FromText(_ & "-01"))}}),
Merged = Table.NestedJoin(Actuals, {"MonthName"}, Targets, {"Month"}, "T", JoinKind.LeftOuter)
```
Why will this fail when more months are added, and what is the correct join key approach?
options: Different years share the same month name; use a start-of-month Date key on both tables and join on that.
It won't fail; month names are stable. Keep as is.
`Date.FromText(_ & "-01")` is invalid. Use `Date.From` instead and keep joining on names.
Join on `Date.Year([OrderDate])` only; targets are annual by nature.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Joining on month names conflates months across years. Create a proper start-of-month Date (e.g., `Date.StartOfMonth([OrderDate])` and `Date.FromText(Month & "-01")`) and join on that key to keep year and month together.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A ignores the year dimension and will misjoin. C focuses on a parsing function but preserves the flawed key. D throws away month granularity entirely.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You have a staging/cleaning pattern:

```powerquery
Source_Sales  // loads raw
Clean_Sales = let
  Source = Source_Sales,
  Trimmed = Table.TransformColumns(Source, {{"Customer", Text.Trim}}),
  Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Trimmed, {{"OrderDate", type date}})
in
  Typed
```
You disable load on `Source_Sales` and only load `Clean_Sales`. What is the effect on the model and refresh?
options: No change to `Clean_Sales`; disabling load only hides `Source_Sales` from the model but it still refreshes as a dependency.
`Clean_Sales` will refresh but `Source_Sales` will not refresh, risking stale data.
Refresh stops entirely; at least one loaded query must read the source.
`Clean_Sales` will error because `Source_Sales` is disabled for load.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Disabling load affects visibility in the model, not dependency execution. `Source_Sales` still refreshes behind the scenes because `Clean_Sales` depends on it.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A confuses load with availability; references still work. C is false; dependencies can be all connection-only except for the final loaded query. D misunderstands dependency refresh; dependencies refresh with their dependents.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Stakeholder note in the draft spec:

```text
KPI: Revenue Growth >= 10%.
Notes: Use "Net Sales" from ERP export (excludes returns). Multi-currency present. Refresh: monthly, at month close.
```
Which missing decision must be nailed down in requirements to make this KPI computable in your preparation workflow without rework later?
options: Commit to a specific dashboard layout for KPI placement so users can find it.
Define the comparison basis (e.g., vs prior month or prior year) and the exact period alignment for month close.
Choose a color palette for positive/negative growth to ensure stakeholder buy-in.
Decide whether to publish to Power BI Service or share PBIX by email.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Without a clearly defined comparison basis and period alignment, the growth calculation is ambiguous. The prep workflow must aggregate to the correct period and produce the right keyed periods to compare.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B and C are presentation concerns, not blockers for computability. D is about distribution; it does not resolve the KPI’s definitional ambiguity.

scenario_questions.scenario:
You are scoping a first-release operations dashboard. Stakeholders propose these KPIs and constraints:

```text
Scope: Customer Support function
Stakeholders: Head of Support, QA Lead
Refresh: Daily at 07:00 from the ticketing database dump (CSV), appended daily
Fields available in dump: TicketID, CreatedAt, FirstResponseAt, ClosedAt (nullable), Status, Priority, Channel, AssignedAgent
Constraints: No changes to source system. Time zone alignment must be UTC. Weekends should be excluded from "Backlog Age" metrics.
Proposed KPIs:
K1. Average Resolution Time (hours)
K2. % Tickets Breached SLA (first response > 4 business hours)
K3. Backlog Age (median days open of all open tickets)
K4. Tickets per Agent per Day
```
There is no semantic model yet; you can only rely on Power Query transformations and well-defined aggregates.
scenario_questions.task: Decide which KPIs are safe to include in v1 given the data and constraints. For each included KPI, specify the exact computable definition, data filters, time handling, and any exclusions. For any KPI you exclude from v1, state the blocker and what would unblock it. Justify your choices briefly, pointing to the available fields and constraints.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: A strong answer includes K1, K2, and K3 with defensible, computable definitions and defers K4 or qualifies it. Example: include K1 as average of (ClosedAt - CreatedAt) in hours, filter Status = Closed, compute in UTC, exclude weekends only if specifically required; since K1 is wall-clock, weekend exclusion not applied unless requested. Include K2 as percentage of tickets where (FirstResponseAt - CreatedAt) > 4 business hours; define business hours rule or state blocker: without business-hours calendar, approximate by excluding weekends using a custom function or defer until calendar is available; acceptable answer either formalizes a reasonable business-hours approximation in PQ or explicitly defers K2 noting the missing calendar. Include K3 as median of (Now or day-end - CreatedAt) for Status != Closed; explicitly exclude weekends in age calculation per requirement using a documented approximation or argue for deferral until a business-day function is approved. For K4, flag blocker: lacks per-day staffing or shifts; raw fields do not include Agent working time, so "per Day" must be clarified (by CreatedAt date? closed date?), and double counting across days must be addressed. Each decision ties to fields present and constraints like UTC and CSV appends.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identify v1-feasible KPIs versus those needing additional data or rules, with justification tied to available fields
For each included KPI, provide an explicit, computable definition (aggregation, filters, time basis, units)
Address time handling (UTC, weekend exclusion) consistently and realistically (approximation or deferral stated)
State clear blockers and concrete unblockers for any deferred KPI(s)

scenario_questions.scenario:
ETL draft for Sales uses SQL plus CSV targets. Current M steps (simplified):

```powerquery
let
  SQL = Sql.Database("bi", "Sales"),
  Fact = SQL{[Schema="dbo", Item="FactSales"]}[Data],
  Filtered = Table.SelectRows(Fact, each [OrderDate] >= #date(2026,1,1)),
  Merged = Table.NestedJoin(Filtered, {"ProductID"}, Products, {"ProductID"}, "P", JoinKind.LeftOuter),
  Expanded = Table.ExpandTableColumn(Merged, "P", {"Category"}, {"Category"}),
  AddedIndex = Table.AddIndexColumn(Expanded, "Idx", 1, 1, Int64.Type),
  Grouped = Table.Group(AddedIndex, {"Category"}, {{"Sales", each List.Sum([Amount]), type number}})
in
  Grouped
```
Performance is poor and DBA reports heavy data pulled from SQL. Products is an Excel query already cleaned. You must preserve folding for SQL-side filtering and joining where possible.
scenario_questions.task: Propose a revised step sequence that maximizes folding and minimizes data pulled from SQL. Explain which steps fold and why, and where to place any non-folding steps. Consider whether to pre-stage `Products` into SQL semantics (e.g., via staging table) or how to handle an Excel dimension in a way that avoids exploding rows on the server. Provide the revised M outline and rationale.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Expected: Push filters and supported joins before any non-folding transforms. Since joining a SQL table to an Excel table in PQ prevents server-side join, propose either: 1) stage Products in SQL (outside PQ) and then join in-fold; or 2) pre-aggregate/filter Fact in-fold first (e.g., project needed columns, filter date), then materialize (first non-folding step), then merge with Excel locally. Move `Table.AddIndexColumn` and `Table.Group` after folding boundary. Suggested M: Filter Fact; select needed columns; optionally summarize in SQL by Category if a SQL view exists; otherwise keep row-level until after merge; if Excel merge must be local, ensure the SQL query is minimized (date filter and projection) before materialization. Explanation should name `AddIndex` and `Group` as non-folding, and explain that cross-source joins cannot fold to SQL.

rubric.criterion: Revised step order that preserves folding for filters/projections and defers non-folding steps
Correct reasoning about why cross-source joins block folding and how to mitigate
Concrete M outline reflecting the proposal
Awareness of trade-offs (staging dimension vs local merge) and data volume control

scenario_questions.scenario:
Two systems report "Active Users" differently:

```text
Product DB (daily snapshot): UserID, LastLoginAt
CRM (license file): UserID, LicenseStatus (Active/Inactive), LicenseExpiry
Requirement draft: "Active Users (Monthly)" should be one KPI used by Finance and Product.
Conflicts: Some users logged in after license expiry (grace period), some have active licenses but never logged in this month.
```
You must define a single KPI for v1 that both teams will accept, using only Power Query and monthly refresh at period close.
scenario_questions.task: Choose a defensible definition for "Active Users (Monthly)" given the two sources. Specify the join rules, period alignment, edge-case handling (grace period, never-logged-in but licensed), and which table is authoritative for each judgement. Justify how your definition supports consistent month-over-month comparisons and call out any caveats you will document in the dashboard specification.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Good answers define a month-close snapshot KPI like: users counted as active if LicenseStatus = Active as of month end AND LastLoginAt within the month (intersection) to satisfy both Finance (entitlement) and Product (usage). Explain start-of-month and end-of-month keys using `Date.StartOfMonth/EndOfMonth` to align periods. Describe a Left Outer join from CRM to Product DB on UserID; apply filters: license active as of month end (expiry >= EOM), and last login >= SOM and <= EOM. Treat grace period explicitly: either extend expiry by grace days (documented) or exclude such users and note the caveat. rubric.criterion: Clear, defensible KPI definition tying to both entitlement and usage, with period alignment
Correct join/filter logic and treatment of edge cases (grace period, never-logged-in)
Justification that addresses stakeholder needs and comparability over time
Stated caveats/assumptions to include in the specification
